answer_text:
Assuming \(x\) is a fixed real number, we use the elementary bound

\[
|\sin(kx)|\le 1 \qquad \text{for every } k\in\mathbb{N}.
\]

Hence

\[
\left|\sin x\sin(2x)\cdots \sin(nx)\right|
\le 1.
\]

Therefore,

\[
|f_n|
=
\frac{e^x}{\sqrt n}
\left|\sin x\sin(2x)\cdots \sin(nx)\right|
\le
\frac{e^x}{\sqrt n}.
\]

Since \(e^x\) is a finite positive constant and

\[
\lim_{n\to\infty}\frac{e^x}{\sqrt n}=0,
\]

the squeeze theorem gives

\[
\lim_{n\to\infty} f_n=0.
\]

\[
\boxed{0}
\]
